chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhal narrated from Muhammad ibn Khalid from Saif ibn Amirah from Ishaq ibn Ammar from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:

I said to him: A man divorced his wife, then took her back with witnesses, then divorced her, then it occurred to him so he took her back with witnesses, then divorced her, then took her back with witnesses. Is she completely divorced from him? He said: Yes. I said: All of that was in one period of purity? He said: She is completely divorced from him. I said: If he did that with a pregnant woman, is she completely divorced from him? He said: This is not like that.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: The meaning in this report is that if he divorces her three times in one period of purity, with two revocations in between according to the Sunnah, then she is completely divorced from him by the third, as we have mentioned, even if he had not consummated the marriage with her, because whenever he takes her back, it is permissible for him to divorce her another time according to the Sunnah, as we explained. And that is not found in the pregnant woman, because the pregnant woman, when he takes her back, it is not permissible for him to divorce her another time according to the Sunnah until she gives birth to what is in her womb. And it is only permissible for him to divorce her for the waiting period if he has intercourse with her after the revocation, according to what we will explain the statement about, God willing. And this does not contradict this report.

key_terms.رَجْعَة: Revocation (taking back the wife during the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: Does triple divorce in one period of purity apply equally to pregnant and non-pregnant women in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani clarifies the distinction between 'sunna' divorce (one revocable divorce per waiting period) and 'non-sunna' divorce (three in one period) by examining the procedural constraints on revocation. It highlights a key Shia juristic nuance: while a non-pregnant woman allows for immediate subsequent revocations within the same 'tuhr', a pregnant woman’s waiting period (iddah) is tied to childbirth, altering the mechanics of how the third divorce is finalized and rendered irrevocable (tabin).
